author: sonnet
label: c2-seed-sonnet-01
changes: Rewrote the whole file in the skill's layout: summary, terms, diagram, numbered steps, shared rules, open questions.
Defined the terms (event, subscription, delivery, dispatcher, worker, lease, dead letter) and listed the deliveries columns (Q1, Q2, Q4, Q5, Q7).
Explained why retry state is in Postgres: the queue's maximum delay is 15 minutes (Q5).
Made the dispatcher insert with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING and then ack, and stated what happens on a duplicate or a failure (Q3).
Chose the lease as next_attempt_at plus 60 s, with SKIP LOCKED claiming, and the crash recovery that follows (Q4).
Spelled out the 8-attempt schedule and the full result table, including 3xx and other non-2xx as permanent failures with no redirects (Q5, Q6).
Made dead letter a status on the same row (Q7).
Added a lazy subscription check before each send, to handle deliveries waiting for a disabled subscription, plus the rules for new events and re-enabling (Q8).
Specified that replay resets the same row, and that it is refused while the subscription is disabled (Q9).
Specified cleanup: hourly, deleting dead and delivered rows older than 14 days (Q9).
Added a failure-handling line at each step and replaced the old diagram with one that shows the retry loop, the 410 disable and the replay.
Added open questions: the queue dead-letter threshold N, admin API authentication, and a crash-looping delivery.
Step 3: delivery is looked up by subscription_id, uses current status, url and secret, and the core database read has a 5 s timeout (answers the lease and hang question).
Lease term: mentions the 5 s core database read timeout alongside the 10 s request timeout.
Step 1: states one uncached core database query per message.
Step 4: body is the whole event JSON, sent with Content-Type: application/json; a resend has the same id but a new t and signature.
Step 5: spelled out that the wait is chosen by the new attempt_count, so the 6 h wait follows failure 7 only; a failed result write means the same attempt number is sent again.
Step 2: noted that attempt_count is only written after a result, so a crash resend keeps the attempt number.
Step 6: support staff are the callers, list takes a subscription id, replay takes one delivery id.
Open questions: added who sets the queue visibility timeout.
Lease term and step 2: stated that a leased row has a future next_attempt_at and so is not claimable, to answer how leased rows are told apart from due ones.
Step 5: the result write only applies while the row is still pending, so a stalled worker cannot overwrite a result another worker already recorded.
Step 1: added a 5 s timeout on the dispatcher's core database query; a timeout means no ack.
Step 3: disabled-subscription dead-letter is not an attempt, leaves attempt_count and last_status_code alone, and shows in the admin list with its last_error.
Step 4: said the signed bytes are the stored body exactly as sent and described how a receiver verifies.
Step 6: replay returns 404 for an unknown delivery and 409 when the row is not dead or the subscription is disabled.
Open questions: added how customers get their webhook secret.
Step 1: added what happens on a crash between commit and ack, and that a malformed message is simply not acked.
Terms: noted that a message over 256 KB cannot arrive because it is the queue's limit.
Step 2: batch of up to 20 rows per poll, sent in parallel, next poll after the batch finishes, so the batch stays inside the 60 s lease; added a partial index to the columns note.
Step 3: stated that an unreadable core database leaves attempt_count unchanged and repeats every 60 s until it recovers.
Step 4: added handling of a decrypt failure (leave the row, no attempt counted) and what a receiver must do to dedupe, including the effect on replays.
Step 5: a failed subscription disable write on 410 does not stop the delivery from being dead-lettered.
Open questions: merged the crash-loop item with the unreadable-database and decrypt cases.
Merged the repeated failure handling into a bullet list under each step, so each failure appears once, where it happens.
Added a short definition of the queue dead-letter topic to the terms and why our dead letters are table rows. This answers the questions about malformed messages and the queue's dead-letter topic.
Folded the lease explanation into one term, with the claimable condition (pending and due) stated there. Step 2 now shows the 15 s worst case as 5 s read plus 10 s POST.
Moved the receiver verification and dedupe explanation into step 4, with the replay effect on receivers. Step 5 points back to step 4 instead of repeating it.
Moved the decrypt-failure rule into step 4 as a sub-bullet. Moved the unreadable-core-database rule into step 3.

Cut repetition: the long 'this is how waiting deliveries are handled' wording, the repeated restatement of lease and crash behaviour, and the Q/A-style justifications. Kept every number, limit, header, status code, schedule and rule.
Made the diagram the visual centre: the summary and terms come first, then the diagram, then the steps. Steps add only what the diagram cannot show.
Added no new mechanism. There was no build or rollout content in the first version, so no separate rollout section was needed.
Left out details nothing asked for, such as library or exact format choices. The open questions are unchanged.
